pr_title: Add support for index_filter to open pit
pr_body:
The open point in time API accepts a list of indices and opens a point in time view against those indices. Like we do already for field caps, this commit allows users to provide an index_filter parameter as part of the request body, that will be used to execute the can match phase and exclude the indices that can't possibly match such filter.

Closes #99740
pr_comments: Hi @javanna, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: Incorporate can-match phase into PIT creation
issue_context.body:
When a user creates a PIT today they will often have a good sense of the queries for which they will be using it, and in particular all those queries may target a very limited time range. However the PIT will be created to target entire data streams, many of whose backing indices will not match any of the future queries, so Elasticsearch does unnecessary work creating the PIT on shards that will never contain any matches, and further unnecessary work re-running the can-match phase on all those shards for every search.

IMO it would be good if the creation of a PIT could include a filter, and we ran the can-match phase up-front while creating the PIT to limit the shards it targets. We'd need to make it an error if searches using the PIT did not include the same filter (or perhaps something more restrictive).

Relates https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/99739 in that this would substantially reduce the size of PIT IDs in many cases.
comments: We have a list of enhancements for PIT in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/96775, but only one of them has been implemented.

review_comments: What we want here is to check if the index filter exists / or is a not just match-all query (since we explicitly set `source` above) and if so, continue the standard process flow and let it take care of the query attached to `source`, right?  Just for my understanding, why do we return a `CanMatchPreFilterSearchPhase` here if there is no filter (or a match-all) ?

> why do we return a CanMatchPreFilterSearchPhase here if there is no filter (or a match-all) ?

That should not be what's happening. The intention is to run the can match phase only when it makes sense (when there is an index filter which may rewrite to match_none), otherwise skip the can match phase entirely (else branch). 

If there is not index_filter, or if the index_filter is a match_all query (it is impossible for it to hold suggest or aggs), the canRewriteToMatchNone will return false, hence we will skip the can match phase. Does this make sense?
Yeah makes sense, thanks @javanna ! (somehow I was confused :/ - apologies for the noise!)
